summary.text: Lauren Underwood is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 14th District and a registered nurse, and she won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

Before her first election in 2018 she was a senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and taught nursing students at Georgetown University. Her official biography lists her work on the House Appropriations Committee and her role as co-founder of the Black Maternal Health Caucus.

paragraphs.text: Underwood was born in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, and graduated from Neuqua Valley High School in Naperville, Illinois; according to Wikipedia, her family moved to Naperville when she was three and she graduated in 2004.
She earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan in 2008 and a master's degree from Johns Hopkins University in 2009.

A registered nurse, she became a senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in 2014 (per Wikipedia), where her official biography says she helped communities prepare for and respond to disasters, bioterror threats and public health emergencies and helped implement the Affordable Care Act.

According to her official biography, she also taught future nurse practitioners through Georgetown University's online master's program and worked with a Medicaid plan in Chicago on care quality and cost efficiency.
Underwood announced her candidacy in August 2017, won the 2018 Democratic primary, and defeated Republican incumbent Randy Hultgren in the November 2018 general election with 52.5% of the vote.

She was sworn in on January 3, 2019, and her official biography describes her as the first woman, first person of color and first millennial to represent the district. She was re-elected in 2022 (54.2%) and 2024 (55.1%).
She won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 62.6% of the vote to James Marter's 37.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
She serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and is Co-Chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.
Underwood co-founded and co-chairs the Black Maternal Health Caucus. Her official biography describes her as a lifelong Girl Scout and says she lives in Naperville, Illinois.
